newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hurricane Dolly a blessing to parched Nuevo Leon.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Dolly a blessing to parched Nuevo Leon.

text.p: Hurricane Dolly left parched Nuevo Leon state with about 183 million cubic yards (140 million cubic meters) of water, making it "a great blessing" for the state, Governor Benjamin Clariond said on Wednesday.
Agriculture in this primarily industrial state has been devastated by cylical droughts in recent years.
The Atlantic hurricane struck Mexico last month, leaving two dead.

El Cuchillo dam, the largest in the state, retained 154 million cubic yards (118 million cubic meters) of water because of Dolly, Clariond said. As of September 9, El Cuchillo had 413 cubic yards (316 million cubic meters) of water, Clariond told reporters during a meeting of the state agricultural cabinet.
He attributed figures to the National Water Commission.
